decisions.reason: The original Definition calls all three formulas statistics on the observed sample space, although Greenwood is undefined when n=1 and an event occurs by t: Y=Delta N=1 makes Y(Y-Delta N)=0. The cited statistic interface requires a total measurable map. Repaired by distinguishing the measurable Greenwood formula on its measurable positive-denominator domain from its explicitly defined zero extension on the whole sample space; the extension has no variance interpretation outside that domain.

reviews.reason: Reviewed right-censoring and statistic suppliers, owning page and contract, finite endpoint/tie/count conventions and direct consumer uses. At event times 1<=Delta N<=Y, so Nelson-Aalen and Kaplan-Meier have valid finite Borel formulas on every sample. Finite comparisons select one representative per tied event and test the Greenwood domain, so this domain is Borel and the zero extension is a total real-valued measurable statistic. Empty event sets give (Lambda,S,V)=(0,1,0); complete risk-set failure leaves the raw Greenwood formula undefined and its extension zero. No choice principle or new prerequisite is needed. This is the repair author's verification, not independent rejudgment.

interface_change.before: For each fixed $t$, these are statistics of the observed sample in the sense of [[def-statistic-and-estimator]]. To express event-time sums and products as fixed finite operations, scan indices $i=1,\ldots,n$ and include only the first event observation at each distinct time; each inclusion condition uses finitely many Borel equalities and inequalities among the observed $U_i$ and $\delta_i$. Risk and event counts are finite Borel sums, and every division uses the stated positive-count branch. Greenwood is defined only on its positive-denominator domain.
interface_change.after: Nelson-Aalen and Kaplan-Meier are total statistics; Greenwood is measurable on D_n(t), and V_G^circ(t) is its total zero extension.
interface_change.preserved: All estimator formulas, endpoints, ties, positive-domain restriction, discrete/continuous targets, and absence of a finite-sample variance identity remain unchanged.
